decisions.executionNote: Holder is in the right workspace; orient right hand for a side grasp while leaving left hand clear. Small initial motions preserve elbow-up continuity.
Advance the right hand toward the holder from its right side, finishing the inward-facing orientation. Keep the gripper open and approach above the table.
After the continuity rejection, hold orientation and use smaller inward/forward increments to approach the holder without changing wrist branch.
Bring the open right fingers around the holder side at mid-height, maintaining the established elbow-up branch.
Holder shifted slightly during approach. Withdraw sideways before correcting forward alignment, avoiding another push with the open finger.
Approach the now-visible holder slowly from the right with a small forward and upward correction before closing.
Cup remains off-center toward the forward finger. Back off before a forward-only correction, then reassess the opening alignment.
Move inward and slightly forward to enclose the holder, then close. Holder tilt and wrist-camera offset make retention uncertain; verify before transport.
The holder has toppled and is not retained. Open and lift clear to prepare a controlled recovery grasp rather than continuing to push it.
Reorient the raised right wrist toward an overhead recovery grasp, moving above the fallen holder with open fingers and conservative rotation.
Previous motion was rejected without execution. Reduce wrist increments substantially and gain clearance before continuing recovery.
Continue the overhead recovery orientation at clearance, centering the right wrist over the fallen cup.
Replan from the interrupted prefix: retreat slightly toward the robot and lower the wrist while rotating slowly toward a downward recovery grasp.
Align the downward-facing right gripper above the fallen holder body. Maintain an open aperture and stop above contact for visual correction.
The forward rotation approached a continuity limit. Keep the accepted orientation and lower slowly toward the cup body, reducing reach before any further wrist rotation.
Correct forward and downward toward the fallen cup body. The wrist view indicates the cup is still beyond the grasp center; keep fingers open during alignment.
The reach limit interrupted forward travel. Withdraw toward the robot while tilting the approach forward, creating reach margin for a diagonal grasp rather than extending farther.
No motion executed in the rejected chunk. Use submillimeter retreat and very small rotations initially to move away from the near-extension singularity continuously.
Head view now places the fingers across the fallen cup. Make a small centering correction, close fully, and perform a short lift toward the robot to test retention.
The test closure was empty. Reopen and place the fingers deeper and farther forward around the cup body before closing again.
Test retention with a closed-gripper lift toward the robot, moving away from the reach limit. Use the resulting cup motion to distinguish a grasp from contact.
The lift was empty. Align a more vertical grasp across the cup near its nearer end, rather than approaching its side obliquely.
Use translation only after the rejected rotation, lowering the open fingers in small steps toward the near end of the cup.
Advance the open grasp center farther forward at constant height; the fallen holder is still beyond the fingertips rather than between them.
Forward reach hit the continuity guard. Retract the wrist and angle the fingers more forward, allowing a cup grasp with the wrist farther inside the reachable workspace.
Continue the forward-angled recovery approach with the wrist safely retracted, bringing the open fingers across the fallen holder body.
Cup is now centered laterally in the wrist view. Move slightly deeper around its body and close fully, then verify with a separate lift.
The cup now appears enclosed between the fingers. Keep fully closed and lift toward the robot to verify retention and gain clearance for uprighting.
The cup was not retained. Reopen and descend around its nearer body section at the current forward-angled orientation, avoiding another forward push.
Cup is centered between the open jaws. Lower slightly for side contact, close fully, and make a short vertical retention test.
Cup appears enclosed at both sides. Keep the grasp fully closed and lift/retract into a safer workspace before attempting to upright it.
Cup slipped during the larger lift but is now closer and reachable. Reopen and descend deeper around its sides, rather than pinching the upper face.
Center the pinch farther along the cup body, close fully, and lift vertically only to avoid dragging it out of a shallow grasp.
Maintain the deeper closed grasp and lift straight upward slowly. Check that the cup rises with the fingers before rotating it upright.
Keep the jaws closed while slowly raising and uprighting the cup. Some sliding is visible, so use a small rotation and reassess retention.
The cup slipped free and is now nearer the robot. Use the improved reach to prepare a truly downward grasp across its body, with the fingers open.
Finish orienting the jaws downward and align above the cup's nearer half, using small continuous increments.
Descend the vertical jaws around the holder sidewalls, make a small centering correction, then close fully without dragging.
Maintain the full closure and lift the deeper vertical grasp gently, with only a small retreat to preserve reach margin.
Cup now rises with the deeper grasp. Keep closed and rotate its long axis toward upright while retracting the wrist away from the reach limit.
Maintain the retained cup and finish uprighting it while lifting clear and shifting slightly right. Verify the mouth orientation before transferring pens.
Cup is retained, but the mouth orientation is obscured. Move to a right-side holding position and turn gradually to expose it to the head view before insertion.
The exposed flat hexagon confirms the holder is inverted. Finish the side-facing pose at clearance, then roll the retained holder over to put its mouth upward.
Roll the securely held inverted cup around the right grasp axis toward upright. Begin the left hand's inward orientation for pen pickup without crossing workspaces.
Continue the retained cup's roll past sideways. Move the left hand above the leftmost cyan pen and gradually orient its jaws downward along the pen.
Bring the cup mouth fully upward and lower it to an accessible holding height while the left hand approaches the first cyan pen from above.
The holder mouth is visibly upright. Keep it closed in the right hand at a lower insertion height and center the left jaws around the first cyan pen.
Use the left wrist view to center the pen laterally between the jaws, then close and make a small lift. Hold the upright cup stationary.
Lift the centered cyan pen and rotate it toward tip-up while moving within the left workspace. Keep both grasps closed; verify the pen rises with the hand.
The first pen lift was empty. Return with a deeper, slightly corrected grasp. Lower the slipping cup toward table support while continuing to hold it closed.
Close the deeper pen grasp and test a straight lift. The holder has tilted onto its side; keep closed and gently lift/rotate its mouth upward again.
The requested cup tilt was rejected with zero execution. Back the right wrist away from its roll limit using small reverse increments while testing the pen grasp.
The cyan pen is visibly lifted now. Raise and orient it upright while cautiously tilting the cup mouth upward away from the right wrist roll limit.
Replan from the two executed steps. Back the right roll well away from its limit before tilting the cup; continue the retained pen's lift without crossing arms.
The pen is retained. Finish its upright orientation while pitching the sideways cup mouth upward, with the right wrist roll now away from its limit.
The pitch command was rejected before execution. Reduce pitch sharply and turn the right wrist away from its side-facing singularity while the left hand finishes the pen orientation.
Hold the nearly upright pen stationary after the left-arm guard. Pitch the cup mouth upward in smaller increments from the less singular right-hand orientation.
The right pitch developed tracking lag near its wrist limit. Raise the retained cup without further rotation to gain joint margin, keeping the pen steady and separate.
The lift was rejected before execution. Start with a much smaller upward increment to bridge the previous target residual, then raise continuously without changing orientation.
With wrist margin restored, rotate the cup mouth upward while raising the wrist to avoid the flexion limit. Keep the upright pen clear and stationary.
Right wrist roll is near its limit. Unwind about the current grasp axis with the cup retained, preserving position and elbow configuration before further uprighting.
The holder axis is now nearly upright after unwinding. Make a small final roll correction and lower slightly while bringing the retained pen higher and vertical for insertion.
The cup opening remains hidden despite an upright-looking silhouette. Roll it toward the head camera to identify the mouth unambiguously, retaining the pen in the left hand.
Right wrist flexion is saturating again. Remove the oblique wrist tilt while retracting slightly, preserving the grasp and avoiding additional pitch into the limit.
The holder mouth is now visibly upright. Freeze the right grasp and bring the retained vertical pen higher and toward the opening, keeping left EE on its own side.
Translate the upright pen over the visible holder mouth, keeping its lower end above the rim until horizontally centered. Right hand remains fixed and closed.
Lower the pen vertically toward the centered opening with a tiny lateral correction, keeping the grasp closed until the lower end is visibly inside.
The pen's lower end is visibly inside the mouth. Seat it a little deeper, release, and withdraw leftward/upward while the right hand stabilizes the holder.
One cyan pen remains upright in the holder after release. Withdraw and orient the left hand for the second cyan pen lying farther forward, holding the cup steady.
The holder tipped during withdrawal and appears to have slipped toward the right fingertips. Freeze the left hand and re-seat the right grasp farther around the holder body before moving away.
The cup fell but the inserted pen remains inside. Clear the left hand and prepare an overhead right-hand recovery grasp across the cup body, avoiding the exposed pen.
No recovery motion executed after the guard. Start the right reorientation much more slowly while raising for wrist margin; withdraw the left hand well clear.
Continue the overhead recovery orientation while approaching above the cup body. Keep clear of the protruding cyan pen and preserve the current elbow branch.
Center a vertical right-hand grasp over the fallen holder, away from the protruding pen. Descend only to the sidewall approach height before closing.
Descend around both cup sidewalls, close fully, and test a short vertical lift. The cyan pen still protrudes from the mouth, so avoid dragging.
Lift the deep cup grasp and rotate its pen-protruding end upward, rather than raising the closed base. Keep the inserted cyan pen inside during recovery.
The backward-facing tilt reached a wrist limit. Retract into the reachable workspace and yaw the held cup toward a side-facing uprighting path instead.
Bring the cup mouth upward through a combined yaw/pitch path with the wrist retracted. Keep the deep grasp closed and retain the cyan pen inside.
Continue the same smooth uprighting arc. The cyan pen remains inside the visible opening; keep the deeper holder grasp closed throughout.
Replan from the interrupted prefix with smaller cup rotations. Move the holder rightward while bringing its mouth nearly upright, without driving the wrist to its roll limit.
The recovered cup still contains the first pen. Lower it toward a supported holding height while positioning the left hand above the remaining cyan pen.
Finish the downward pen approach while lowering the cup close to table support. Keep the cup firmly enclosed and the left jaws open for final visual alignment.
The vertical pen approach hit the reach guard. Angle the fingers forward while retracting/lowering the wrist, so the grasp reaches the pen without extending the arm farther.
Advance the angled left fingers slightly farther along the cyan pen and lower for a deeper centered pinch, then close fully before lifting.
Lift the now-enclosed second cyan pen and rotate it toward upright, retracting the wrist to preserve reach margin. Keep the supported holder fixed.
The second pen is visibly retained. Finish rotating it upright and position above the supported cup opening before descending.
